messages:
simon: Heads up — after the 565 driver rollout to canary pool in us-west2 we're seeing NCCL init failures on startup for some instance types. Anyone else?
maya: yep, spotted ~12 nodes with CUDA errors during provisioning, a few stuck in 'provisioning' state.
kevin: logs?
simon: paste from one of the nodes:
```
[  +0.567890] nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel.
[  +1.234567] NVRM: GPU 0000:01:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed!
[  +1.345678] nvidia-nvlink: probing failed
[  +1.456789] NCCL WARN Call to cudaGetDeviceCount failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
```
dalia: also seeing dkms build failures on node bootstrap:
```
DKMS: build started for nvidia/565-0ubuntu1
make: Entering directory '/usr/src/nvidia-565'
make: *** No rule to make target 'modules'.  Stop.
ERROR (dkms apport): kernel package linux-headers-5.15.0-xyz not installed
```
maya: interestingly this is mostly on older kernel hosts (5.15). eu-west1 (newer kernels) looks fine. probably header mismatch + new kernel ABI with 565.
kevin: infra-bot deploy log shows the canary only had 20% of nodes upgraded, but our auto-scale moved some older-kernel nodes into the canary subgroup.
infra-bot: deploy: driver/565 rollout started -> canary group (20%); region: us-west2; started_by: @simon
simon: ok that explains cluster mixing. can we cordon older-kernel nodes from canary until we verify header compatibility?
dalia: we should also check NCCL/CUDA runtime versions in the image. 565 needs CUDA 11.8+ — images with 11.7 may break.
maya: confirmed — image on the problematic fleet is CUDA 11.7. eu-west1 images were rebuilt with 11.8 last week.
kevin: options: 1) revert canary to 550 (fast), 2) rebuild images in us-west2 with CUDA 11.8 and headers (longer), 3) pin canary to newer kernel hosts only.
ops-oncall: revert sounds fastest to reduce capacity impact. how many nodes are unhealthy?
maya: ~12 unhealthy, ~6 still provisioning, 4 reprovision loops. impact: about 3% of capacity in us-west2 degraded.
dalia: rollback cost estimate: small (no infra change), but delays driver validation. Rebuild images cost: ~2-4 hours image build + deploy across pool, but will be safer going forward.
simon: given this is canary, revert to 550 for now and we do a targeted image rebuild/pinning. I'll trigger rollback.
infra-bot: action: rollback driver -> 550 initiated by @simon at 1756001800.
kevin: also add pre-check: before any driver rollouts, validate kernel-headers and CUDA runtime presence in node metadata. simple script run by the deploy pipeline.
dalia: I can add a dkms preflight check to fleet-provisioner (check /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build and /usr/src for nvidia-565).
ops-oncall: schedule: roll back now, reprovision fix in dev for next 2 hours, then small canary re-run tomorrow after image push.
maya: FYI, some NCCL hangs manifested as long tail retries from training jobs — increased job latency and token queue backlog. Investigating job-level retries to avoid double-scheduling.
simon: good catch. Notify customers if SLA hit? current impact is minor but we should monitor.
kevin: putting dashboard alert: GPU provisioning failure rate spike -> page if >5% for 15m.
dalia: I'll open a short postmortem draft after rollback summarizing root cause: driver+cuda+headers mismatch + autoscaler mixing nodes.
simon: thanks team. after rollback we'll add deploy-time gating to prevent heterogeneous kernel/driver combos in a canary.
ops-oncall: tagging follow-ups: @dalia image preflight, @kevin deploy gating, @maya capacity monitoring.
infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-3421 "565 driver canary regen: kernel/header/CUDA mismatch in us-west2" assigned to infra oncall.
kevin: one more note — cost impact minimal today, but repeated rollbacks will add churn. let's avoid region-wide rollouts until image parity is confirmed. :thumbsup:
maya: monitoring line-increased, will update in 20m.
simon: closing loop here for now. thanks. :white_check_mark:
